risk: If implementation follows only the active claim, recursion depth can replace execution-strategy semantics. That would make R1/R2/R3 labels ambiguous and can later corrupt routing, telemetry, method-credit attribution, resume/replacement policy and held-out ablations. A depth ceiling is useful but is not equivalent to the architecture's four strategy classes.
counterhypothesis: The README wording could be stale and the active claim could intentionally redefine WP603. No explicit reconciliation or contract-change record proving such a semantic replacement was observed at this review point.
required_discriminator: Before acceptance, bind one explicit canonical mapping that keeps recursion strategy and nesting depth as separate fields or explicitly reconcile/supersede the README contract.
Tests must prove R1 model-recursion semantics cannot be silently represented as child-depth-1 only.
Tests must prove R2 child-harness selection is distinct from generic depth-2 metadata.
Tests must prove R3 adaptive selection records the selected lower strategy plus its own decision provenance rather than merely meaning depth 3.
DIRECT_SMALL/DELEGATE_BUILD compatibility and ChildResourceBudget.max_nested_depth must constrain execution depth without redefining strategy identity.
Any semantic contract change must be explicitly reconciliation-bound before ACCEPTED_AT_SCOPE.
non_authority_statement: This artifact does not mutate the active WP603 implementation, does not claim the workpackage, does not execute a child/model/tool/provider, and grants no runtime/GRID/GWT/J-Space/training/effect/completion/whole-system credit.
